A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 21-page versions of the same work, including Appendix A.1–A.13. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific content is identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original iNatSounds and XCDC evaluations, ablations, aggregation experiments, and multimodal case studies, including Tables 1–4 and A1–A2.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including AG-CLIP benchmark evaluations and the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: AG-CLIP's audio encoder, GeoCLIP retrieval, auxiliary SINR checklist prediction and loss, and temporal aggregation remain identical in Sections 4 and A.5–A.6.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same iNatSounds and XCDC coverage, spatiotemporal grouping scenarios, movie clips, and appendix multimodal geolocation and retrieval examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including GeoCLAP, Taxabind, regression, classification, species-range methods, and species oracles.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, training settings, distance thresholds, aggregation procedures, and location-gallery evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same encoder, pooling, and gallery ablations, spatial-error analyses, species-diversity and aggregation experiments, movie case studies, and appendix species-affinity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run reporting for benchmark experiments, mean and standard deviation reporting in Tables 1 and A2, and the 100-run species-subset summaries accompanying Table 3.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including Tables 1–4, A1–A2, and the figures. For example, Table 1 reports AG-CLIP median error of 1082±11 km and regional accuracy of 17.2±0.1% in both versions.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup, model definitions, retrieval expression, and mathematical descriptions are identical. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about natural-audio geolocation, species-range guidance, species-rich and aggregated recordings, and multimodal geo-forensics.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning species cues, distribution shift, aggregation benefits, and multimodal inconsistencies are unchanged, as are the geographic-bias and privacy limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information in Sections A.5–A.6 and A.13 are identical. The benchmark and code access links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 74 works and retain identical research positioning. Reference [7] remains the same iNaturalist Sounds dataset paper; only its bibliographic publication metadata changes.

P1.justification: Reference [7] changes from a conference-proceedings description to Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 37, pages 132524–132544 (2024). The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the narrative and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The shorter reference [7] accompanies changes to bibliography spacing and page breaks on pages 10–13. All figures, tables, and main-text and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates one reference's publication metadata and reflows the bibliography. The methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations are identical, so these limited editorial changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
